name: comment
description: Leave a comment on a Bitbucket Cloud pull request's conversation. With no number it finds the open pull request for the branch the workspace is on. This comments; it does not approve, which is a verdict a flow should not cast.

body.description: The comment, as markdown. Whitespace-only is refused: Bitbucket would accept it and post an empty remark.

number.description: The pull request number, which Bitbucket's own API calls its id. Omit to use the open pull request whose source branch is the one the workspace is on, which fails if there is not exactly one.

repo.description: The repository as "workspace/repository". Omit to read it from the origin remote.

output_schema.description: The comment that was posted. `number` is the pull request and `id` is the comment, which are two different numbers and are named the way the rest of these tools name them.

exit_codes.0: success (the comment is on stdout as JSON)
exit_codes.2: invalid input (body is missing or only whitespace, or no number was given and the branch does not identify exactly one open pull request)
exit_codes.3: not found (no such pull request or repository, or no open pull request for the branch)
exit_codes.4: not permitted (the git repository is above the workspace root)
exit_codes.5: unreachable (DNS failure, connection refused, TLS failure, or the transfer timed out)
exit_codes.6: http error (the API answered with a status that is not success, including a refused token)
exit_codes.7: no credential (BITBUCKET_TOKEN is not in this step's environment)
